tested_scope: One self-contained deterministic local claim/idempotency fixture only. Stable effect_identity=E is initially absent. Writer W1 intends payload H1 and invokes an explicitly assumed atomic canonical single-winner primitive P(E,H1); the canonical commit succeeds but W1 loses its acknowledgement. A simultaneous writer W2 with divergent intent H2 invokes P(E,H2) and receives conflict/already-exists because canonical E already contains H1. Before any retry, both actors perform an explicitly assumed authoritative lookup of E. W1 observes canonical H1 matching its intent and classifies the lost acknowledgement as already_committed without a second mutation. W2 observes canonical H1 differing from intended H2 and preserves payload_conflict without overwrite, second create, or compensating mutation. No public-source probe, O/downstream state, other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, real simultaneous repository write, richer-mode arbitration, external coordinator, or optional second leaf was executed.

observations: Under the explicitly assumed atomic single-winner primitive P and authoritative lookup, acknowledgement loss does not require a blind retry: the original winner can classify canonical H1 as its already-committed effect and emit no second mutation.

The simultaneous divergent writer cannot be collapsed into the same idempotent-success class: canonical H1 does not equal intended H2, so the safe local classification remains payload_conflict_preserved with no overwrite or second create.
The composed trace therefore preserves both duplicate suppression for the acknowledgement-lost winner and conflict visibility for the divergent loser, ending with exactly one canonical effect.
inference: Within this exact deterministic model, stable effect identity plus atomic single-winner admission and payload-aware authoritative reconciliation is sufficient to avoid a duplicate after winner acknowledgement loss while also refusing to erase a simultaneous divergent intent. This is conditional architecture evidence only; the fixture does not prove that an allowed zero-cost Chat/repository transport exposes P, conflict semantics, or sufficiently authoritative read-after-write lookup.
